subject: Dedicated capacity discovery - recap & next steps

Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery - recap & next steps
Attachments: finsolve-dedicated-estimate-v1.pdf

Hi Sarah / Ben 

Thanks again for the call today - great to learn more about FinSolve's realtime scoring workload. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please call out anything I missed.

Pain points
- Unpredictable inference costs during market open spikes (15:30-16:30 ET).
- Current latency tail (p95 ~ 400ms) causing UI timeouts for traders.
- Regulatory requirement for data isolation and VPC peering with your analytics cluster.

Current stack
- In-house feature store + TensorFlow models served behind a Kubernetes autoscaling group.
- Frontend makes model calls via internal gateway; peak sustained TPS reported ~220 req/s, bursts up to ~650 req/s for ~20-30 minute windows.

Success criteria (what "good" looks like)
1) 95th p95 latency < 150ms for production scoring requests (end-to-end).
2) Predictable cost within a committed rate (budget certainty for dedicated capacity).
3) VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for key material.
4) Autoscaling/burst must handle 650 req/s spikes while maintaining warm KV caches to avoid cold-start latency.

Why Redwood Dedicated looks like a fit
- Reserved GPU pool (dedicated capacity) gives you predictable throughput and cost controls.
- Smart routing + warm KV caching reduces tail latency and handles burst windows.
- VPC/private deployment options and KMS integrations meet isolation/compliance needs.

Proposed initial config (ballpark to validate)
- Reserved pool: 4xA100-equivalent GPUs (we can size down/up after bench).
- Target sustained throughput: 250 req/s with autoscaling headroom to 700 req/s for 60-minute bursts.
- Warm-cache warmup policy + pre-warming before market open.

Immediate next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with FinSolve infra + Redwood SREs to validate network/KMS/VPC setup (please propose 2x times).
2) Redwood to share a formal pricing estimate + draft mutual action plan (attached).
3) Access request: temporary read-only logs/ingress sample to run a short baseline test (we'll provide exact specs).

If this captures things correctly, can you confirm the success criteria (esp. latency target and burst profile) and share 2x windows for the technical deep-dive next week?

Thanks 

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Marissa 

- thanks for the thorough write-up, looks right. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Latency target: p95 < 150ms is what we want for the trading UI; however for batch model evaluations p95 can be higher. We'll prioritize realtime scoring.
- Peak/burst: the 650 req/s bursts are real - typically ~20-30 minutes and sometimes back-to-back on adjacent days. We need short-term headroom and predictable fallback if exhausted.
- Security: we require SOC2 evidence + VPC peering and KMS integration; please include these in the technical deep-dive agenda.

We can do a technical deep-dive next Tue 4/21 at 10:30am ET or Wed 4/22 at 2:00pm ET. Either works for our infra folks.

I reviewed the attached estimate briefly - looks in range. Happy to review pricing after the tech call.


—Sarah
